content: Piracetam is believed to enhance the metabolism of brain cells under conditions of hypoxia. It has been utilized as a potential intervention to mitigate the negative effects associated with fetal distress during labor. The purpose of this review was to evaluate the impact of piracetam on delivery methods and perinatal morbidity in cases of suspected fetal distress during labor. A search was conducted in the Cochrane Pregnancy and Childbirth Group's Trials Register as of February 15, 2012. The review included randomized controlled trials that compared piracetam with either a placebo or no treatment in the context of suspected fetal distress during labor. Both authors of the review independently assessed the eligibility of studies and the quality of the trials included. Only one study, involving 96 women, met the inclusion criteria. When comparing piracetam to placebo, there was a trend suggesting a reduced need for cesarean section in the piracetam group (risk ratio 0.57, 95% confidence interval 0.32 to 1.03). However, this finding was not statistically significant. Additionally, there were no significant differences between the piracetam and placebo groups in terms of neonatal morbidity, as measured by neonatal respiratory distress, or in Apgar scores. The authors concluded that the current evidence is insufficient to determine the effectiveness of piracetam for managing fetal distress during labor.
